subject: Re: Helios Retail — Integration scope, auth, and model routing decisions
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Torres <eli.torres@heliosretail.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@heliosretail.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Helios Retail integration scope & immediate asks

Hi Eli / Marcus —

Thanks for the productive call today — appreciate the clarity on the search + customer-assist use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move the technical deep-dive forward: 

Key takeaways
- Primary use case: in-product search augmentation (embeddings + reranker) and an in-chat assistant for returns/faq (tool calling for order lookups).
- Latency target: user-facing search/rerank should aim for ~100ms p95 if possible; chat can tolerate higher for complex flows.
- Data residency: production traffic will be US-only for now (no EU residency requirement at launch).

Immediate asks from our side (please confirm):
1) Preferred SDK languages for the integration (we currently support Node, Python, Java; can provide Go + .NET as needed).
2) Auth model preference: API Key, OAuth with customer-managed KMS, or mTLS?
3) Approx traffic shape for the first 3 months: expected QPS, percent of requests that need reranking vs simple embedding lookup, peak concurrent chats.
4) Any required IP / VPC peering constraints (Marcus mentioned a secure VPN option).

Attached: post-call slide deck (architecture options) and a short auth checklist for you to flag constraints.

Proposed next steps
- You confirm the 4 asks above by Wed 1/20.
- Tech deep-dive (30–45m) with your eng leads — propose Thurs 1/21 or Fri 1/22. Link for scheduling: https://redwood.app/sched?invite=helio-tech-deep-dive
- Follow-up from our infra lead (Rishi) with a concrete routing/fallback proposal based on your answers.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: 20270118-helio-postcall-deck.pdf (pdf, 12 slides), 20270118-auth-checklist.csv (csv, 1 page)

From: Eli Torres <eli.torres@heliosretail.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@heliosretail.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Helios Retail integration scope & immediate asks

Thanks Aditya — good notes. Quick answers inline below.

1) SDKs: Node + Python are our primary stacks (Node on the storefront, Python for offline pipelines). Please surface any sample code for both.
2) Auth: we prefer customer-managed API keys rotated via our KMS. mTLS would be a hard requirement only for backend-to-backend PII pipelines; for the initial POC API keys with per-key ACLs are fine.
3) Traffic shape (initial POC):
   - Baseline QPS: 8–12 qps
   - Peak (holiday test): ~120 qps
   - Reranker proportion: ~18% of search requests will trigger reranking in POC
   - Concurrent chat sessions: 25 active users at peak
4) Network / peering: attached is our network requirements doc — we can do a VPN peering or allow a narrow set of public egress IPs. Marcus will coordinate with infra.

We can do the tech deep-dive on Fri 1/22 at 10:00 PT if that works. Marcus will join with our lead eng.

Also, for pricing: can you provide a ballpark for a 4-week POC (including some reserved capacity for peak tests)? We want a number to justify to finance.

Thanks,
Eli
Eli Torres
Head of Search & Personalization
Helios Retail

Attachments: 20270119-network-requirements.docx (docx, network CIDR + firewall lists)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Torres <eli.torres@heliosretail.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 16:18:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed routing + policy config for Helios POC

Eli — thanks for the numbers, that helps. Based on the traffic shape you shared, heres a pragmatic routing + fallback configuration we recommend for the POC. Im keeping it concrete so you can share with your engs.

Goals: meet p95 latency ~100ms for search/rerank while keeping token cost reasonable during peak tests. Support US-only routing and a canary fallback chain if a variant exceeds latencies.

High-level proposal
- Primary model for search embeddings: redwood-embed-lite-2 (quantized) — lower cost, fast inference.
- Reranker: rerankbert-medium (GPU-backed) — run only when candidate set > 8 or when embedding score spread < 0.08 (heuristic).
- Chat assistant: redwood-chat-3b-std for interactive flows (falls back to chat-2b-quant if CPU/GPU capacity constrained).

Routing & policy rules (plain text config sample)
- route_table:
  - name: helio-primary
    condition: region == "us" AND request.type in ["search","rerank"]
    primary_model: redwood-embed-lite-2
    reranker_model: rerankbert-medium
    latency_slo_p95_ms: 100
    fallback_chain: ["rerankbert-medium-quant","redwood-chat-2b-quant"]
    cost_priority: moderate

- fallback_policy:
  - name: high-latency-fallback
    trigger: rolling_p95_latency > 150ms for 1m
    action: divert 20% to lower-cost quant variant, divert 10% to secondary region if available

Operational notes
- Continuous batching: enable adaptive batching with max batch delay = 8ms for search paths.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for frequent queries (TTL 12h).
- Auth: support API keys scoped to routes + IP allowlist. For mTLS pipelines we will provide dedicated VPC routing instructions.

Next steps
1) Eli / Marcus: confirm SDK languages (Node/Python OK) and VPN vs IP allowlist by 1/20 EOD.
2) Well produce a POC config bundle (routing table + sample SDK snippets + IAM example) by 1/21.
3) Schedule POC week: proposed week of Feb 7 — we will pre-provision reserved capacity for peak test windows.

Ive pasted short SDK snippets below (Node + Python) to show the auth header pattern and routing hint header we use. These are intentionally minimal.

Node snippet (pseudo):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, region: 'us' });
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-embed-lite-2', input: 'query text', routing_hint: 'helio-primary' });

Python snippet (pseudo):
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ['RW_API_KEY'], region='us')
res = client.embed(model='redwood-embed-lite-2', text='query text', routing_hint='helio-primary')

If you want, we can include a short demo app repo for Node that wires the SDK into a simple search/rerank pipeline.

- Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Eli Torres <eli.torres@heliosretail.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed routing + policy config for Helios POC

Thanks Rishi — the proposal looks sensible and conservative. A couple quick clarifications:

- Confirmed: Node + Python SDKs are fine. Marcus will follow up on VPN vs IP allowlist by EOD (leaning to IP allowlist for the initial POC).
- POC timing: we can do week of Feb 7 as suggested. Goal: 4-week POC with one peak test week (we'll simulate holiday load).
- Pricing: for finance sign-off we need a ballpark estimate for reserved capacity and peak test usage. Can you provide a 4-week estimate (dev + reserved peak window) by EOD 1/21?

Numbers to confirm from us: an initial conservative peak for the holiday simulation is 150 qps sustained for 1 hour; well provide exact windows next week.

If you can send the POC config bundle and sample Node demo repo by 1/21, well route it to Marcus and our infra lead. Also, please include the minimal NDA and a payment contact for procurement.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Eli
